extraction.name: EgoLife
extraction.description: A comprehensive ultra-long egocentric, interpersonal, multiview, and multimodal daily life dataset with intensive annotation, collected from six participants living together for one week.
extraction.creator: The EgoLife Team
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected over seven days with six volunteers residing in a custom-designed environment called the EgoHouse, wearing Meta Aria glasses for egocentric multimodal capture, with synchronized third-person GoPro cameras and millimeter-wave radars.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: First-person video from AI glasses, third-person video from fixed indoor cameras, and synchronized multimodal signal data including millimeter-wave radars and WiFi signals.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The dataset underwent synchronization, de-identification, audio muting for sensitive information, multimodal signal extraction and alignment, and audio processing for annotation readiness.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Transcript annotations were generated with speech recognition and diarization, then reviewed and refined by reviewers. Caption annotations were created by splitting videos into 5-minute clips, slowing them to 0.8× speed, having annotators provide continuous narrations, transcribing and correcting them, then merging and expanding captions with GPT-4o-mini and GPT-4o and verifying them by human annotators. QA annotations were generated from visual-audio captions with GPT-4o, then filtered, selected, revised, and augmented with distractors by annotators.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: AI-generated QA candidates were filtered to retain only questions requiring information from at least five minutes prior, with preference for longer dependencies and real-world relevance; annotators also marked whether audio was required and the necessary look-back time.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: speech recognition [90], open-source diarization algorithm [91], GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4o
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The work is discussed as potentially improving personalized assistance, daily organization, contextual reminders, education, and professional support, while requiring safeguards for privacy, autonomy, trust, and transparency.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset intentionally starts with a narrow setting, sacrificing some generalizability such as single language and scenario.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset currently has limited generalizability due to its narrow setting, including single language/scenario, and the paper notes plans to expand to broader languages, locations, and activities.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for research on egocentric AI assistants, long-duration activity understanding, interpersonal dynamics, contextual interactions, multimodal signal analysis, human behavior recognition, and long-context question answering benchmarks.

name.evidence: We introduce EgoLife, a project to develop an egocentric life assistant that accompanies and enhances personal efficiency through AI-powered wearable glasses.

description.evidence: This effort resulted in the EgoLife Dataset, a comprehensive 300-hour egocentric, interpersonal, multiview, and multimodal daily life dataset with intensive annotation.

inLanguage.evidence: The primary language of the EgoLife dataset is Chinese1. All the annotations (transcripts, captions, QAs) are primarily in Chinese and translated into English.

isLiveDataset.evidence: This ongoing project aims to document human daily activities in natural environments, advancing research in human behavior recognition, multimodal signal analysis, and human-machine interaction.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: Overview The EgoLife dataset was collected over a seven-day period with six volunteers residing in a custom-designed environment, called the EgoHouse (shown in Figure 1). Each participant wore Meta Aria glasses [1] and captured multimodal egocentric videos. To enhance the dataset with third-person perspectives, 15 strategically placed GoPro cameras recorded the participants’ activities from multiple angles. Additionally, millimeter-wave radars provided spatial and motion data, supporting synchronized, comprehensive multimodal analysis of daily events and interactions.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: We conducted a comprehensive data collection study where six participants lived together for one week, continuously recording their daily activities—including discussions, shopping, cooking, socializing, and entertainment—using AI glasses for multimodal egocentric video capture, along with synchronized third-person-view video references.

Data Instances Each data instance includes:

• Third-person video from fixed indoor cameras

rai:dataCollectionTimeframe.evidence: Overview The EgoLife dataset was collected over a seven-day period with six volunteers residing in a custom-designed environment, called the EgoHouse (shown in Figure 1).

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence:
D.5. Data Preprocessing
Multimodal Signal Extraction Signal data, including radar and WiFi, were extracted and aligned with video data to create a comprehensive multimodal dataset.
Multi-view Synchronization Video and signal data from multiple sources were synchronized using timestamps for cohesive analysis.
De-identification Process All faces and sensitive visual data were blurred. Any sensitive topics in audio were muted to protect participant privacy.
Audio Processing Audio was processed to mute sensitive information and enhance clarity for Q&A annotations.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence:
We started transcript annotation after synchronizing all the egocentric videos, merging audio tracks from six participants into one, and applying speech recognition [90] to generate initial timestamped transcripts. Using an open-source diarization algorithm [91], we differentiated the speakers and produced a preliminary transcript with overlapping conversations.
We split all the videos into 5-minute clips, which were slowed to 0.8 × speed, allowing annotators to provide continuous, detailed narrations by talking without pauses for high information density.
Using GPT-4o-mini, we merged related phrases into 25K “merged captions,” forming coherent sentences aligned with specific video segments. These captions were then expanded by pairing them with representative frames (sampled at 1 FPS) and corresponding transcripts, summarized by GPT-4o. This process transformed the “merged captions” into “visual-audio captions,” which are enriched with both visual and speech context and verified by human annotators.
We crafted prompts for each type and fed “visual-audio captions” into GPT-4o in batches, generating around 100K timestamped questions per participant.
After a rigorous selection and refinement process, we filtered the 100K QA candidates down to 1K high-quality questions per participant—less than 1% of the original pool—for further meticulous revision. This final round of curation resulted in a carefully crafted set of 500 QA per participant. Annotators also generated distractors for multiple-choice questions, formally establishing EgoLifeQA as a benchmark for multiple-choice question answering.

rai:dataAnnotationPlatform.evidence:
The captioning tool is a video editing software with dubbing functions [92].

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence:
Only questions requiring information from at least five minutes prior were retained, with a preference for those demanding longer dependencies and strong real-world relevance.
Annotators also generated distractors for multiple-choice questions, formally establishing EgoLifeQA as a benchmark for multiple-choice question answering. Additionally, they annotated whether audio was required to answer the question and specified the look-back time (certification length) necessary for retrieving the correct answer.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence:
The development of EgoButler and the EgoLifeQA dataset holds significant potential to enhance human-AI interaction, particularly in personalized assistance and context-aware applications.
By enabling AI to understand long-term, egocentric perspectives, EgoButler could support daily activities, personal organization, and contextual reminders, improving quality of life, especially for individuals needing consistent support, such as the elderly or those with cognitive challenges.
However, as this technology integrates more deeply into personal spaces, it is essential to address privacy and ethical considerations to ensure user autonomy and trust. Safeguards for data privacy and transparency in AI decision-making processes will be key to its positive societal reception.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: As the first step toward a realistic egocentric life assistant, we intentionally started with a narrow setting to build a strong foundation, sacrificing some generalizability (e.g., single language/scenario).

rai:dataLimitations.evidence:
As the first step toward a realistic egocentric life assistant, we intentionally started with a narrow setting to build a strong foundation, sacrificing some generalizability (e.g., single language/scenario).
Looking ahead, we plan to expand the dataset to cover a broader range of languages, locations, and activities, and develop more sophisticated models that push the boundaries of AI’s ability to understand and enhance everyday life.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence:
The dataset provides an unprecedented resource for studying long-duration activities, interpersonal dynamics, and contextual interactions, with rich annotations including audio transcript and visual-audio narrations at various time granularity.
This ongoing project aims to document human daily activities in natural environments, advancing research in human behavior recognition, multimodal signal analysis, and human-machine interaction.
Building on the EgoLife dataset, we introduce the EgoLifeQA benchmark, a set of long-context, life-oriented question-answering tasks that assess the effectiveness of personalized AI assistance.
